hero.title: Computers, wiped clean and sent far.
hero.subtitle: We collect used laptops, wipe and re-image them, then send them where they're needed — Wisconsin to Libya to Vietnam. 9 machines in 2022, 56 this season, 156 total.

impact.label: Global reach
impact.text: Every laptop we refurbish reaches a student who wouldn't otherwise have one. This season, 56 machines reached 1,000+ students across four continents.

whyItMatters.heading: Why It Matters
whyItMatters.body: A working laptop isn't a given for a team in Tripoli, Kingston, or Ho Chi Minh City. Libya Team 18422 runs Android Studio on a machine headed for a Wisconsin closet a year earlier — zero cost to the recipient, nothing in a landfill.
whyItMatters.callout: From 9 laptops our first season to 56 this year — an experiment in 2022 is now a supply chain spanning four continents.

pipeline.label: Collect
pipeline.summary: Community drives and partner donations bring machines in.
pipeline.detail: Collection drives run through partners — libraries, Milliman, Reserve Advisors, Soerens Ford — catching machines headed for a closet or landfill. Donors skip the data worries; that's on us.
highlights: Drives with Milliman, Reserve Advisors, Soerens Ford
Collected from individuals, offices, schools in Brookfield
Too old or damaged machines are redirected
Batched intake to match our capacity
No data worries — the wipe is on us

pipeline.label: Inventory
pipeline.summary: Every machine is logged, tested, and triaged before any work begins.
pipeline.detail: Every laptop gets logged and tested first: make, model, RAM, storage, battery, keyboard, screen, ports. What passes moves to the wipe queue; what fails gets reimaged or parted out.
highlights: Logged: make, model, RAM, storage, processor
Full triage: battery, display, keyboard, ports
Clear pass/fail criteria per category
Failed machines recycled, never landfilled
Inventory feeds the distribution match

pipeline.label: Wipe + New OS
pipeline.summary: A clean slate: every drive wiped, every machine re-imaged.
pipeline.detail: The technical core: a multi-pass secure erase, then a fresh OS. FTC-bound machines get activated Windows through Blair Tech, ready for Android Studio. Others get Windows or Linux, tested before it ships.
highlights: Multi-pass erase — zero old data remains
Blair Tech licenses power team-bound machines
Linux on older hardware extends its life
Validated: boot, Wi-Fi, test app
FTC-ready: Android Studio, SDK, build tools

pipeline.label: Distribute
pipeline.summary: Machines matched to recipients and shipped worldwide.
pipeline.detail: Each machine goes to whoever needs what it does — FTC teams need Android Studio horsepower, community programs need something reliable. We coordinate with coaches and Tech Lit Africa's in-country logistics to get machines there intact.
highlights: Matched to each recipient's real needs
FTC-ready machines go to underserved regions first
Shipping coordinated with Tech Lit Africa
Confirmation collected from every recipient
Direct feedback loop once machines arrive
